docs.text: Development For: developers of the page. You'll find: the repository's layout, how the page is put together, trying a change, the vendored libraries, and these docs. The repository Path What ui/console.html The page: HTML, CSS and script in one file, no build ui/vendor/ The two graph libraries, unchanged from npm, and their licences install.py Copies a release into a project, and checks a copy ( Installing ) VERSION The release's version, written into each copy's manifest tests/test_ui.py The page in a real browser against a stand-in server, and the install ( Tests ) .github/workflows/ CI, and publishing these docs docs/ , mkdocs.yml , mkdocs_hooks.py , tools/docs.py These docs, and their site ( below ) LICENSE.txt , NOTICES.txt Apache-2.0; the libraries are MIT How the page is put together One file, in plain JavaScript, with no framework and no build step, so a project serves it as it is. The script, in order: State: the rows, columns and cursor of the latest answer, the tab shown, the features from config.json , and what expanding has added ( extra ). Calls ( call() ): fetch with the key, and an error from the answer's error field. The side panel ( loadSchema() ): from GET /schema , or db.labels() and db.relationshipTypes() . Running ( run() ): the request, the status line, a syntax error's offset. The answer ( render() , showJson() , showProfile() ). The graph views : library() loads a library on first use; gather() finds nodes, relationships and paths anywhere in a row; collect() applies the size limit and adds placeholders; graphData() keeps each node's object between updates so it keeps its place; draw() and expand() . The query box : a transparent <textarea> over a <pre> holding the coloured text, kept the same size and scrolled together; TOKEN splits the text; completions() finds the word before the caret. History , and start() : fetch config.json , hide what the server doesn't have ( data-needs="..." on an element), load the side panel. Why its own query box , of about 100 lines: the usual editor libraries' language modes use a bare name for the language that both projects refuse, and the page would need a build to bundle one. Colours are CSS variables on :root , set again for dark mode; the graph views read them ( tokens() ) when they draw, which is why switching theme draws again. Trying a change The quickest way is the tests' stand-in server, which serves the page with every feature: python -m pytest # everything python -m pytest -k completing # one test To look at it by hand, serve it from a project (install your working copy into it, Installing ), or open a test with Playwright's inspector: PWDEBUG=1 python -m pytest -k expanding . The vendored libraries ui/vendor/README.md lists each file's package, version, licence and SHA-256. To update one: download the package's tarball from registry.npmjs.org, copy dist/<name>.min.js here, update that table and NOTICES.txt if the licence changed, run the tests, and raise VERSION . The page uses: ForceGraph3D / ForceGraph , graphData , nodeId , nodeColor , nodeVal , nodeLabel , linkLabel , linkColor , linkDirectionalArrowLength , linkDirectionalArrowRelPos , cooldownTicks , onNodeClick , onEngineStop , zoomToFit , width , height , backgroundColor , _destructor , and in 3D showNavInfo , nodeResolution and linkOpacity . Check those still work after an update; the tests draw and click in both views. The docs These pages are in docs/ , and published to GitHub Pages at https://sitelabs-com.github.io/sitelabs-graph-ui/ by .github/workflows/mkdocs.yml on every push to main that changes them ( mkdocs gh-deploy to the gh-pages branch). It is the same set-up as sitelabs-partitioned-graph's. Every page starts with a menu , for reading them on GitHub, between `. [tools/docs.py](../tools/docs.py) writes it, and mkdocs.yml 's nav (the site's sidebar), from its GROUPS`; docs/sitedocs.py holds the sections. On the site , mkdocs_hooks.py leaves the menu out (the sidebar is the menu), and points links into the code ( ../install.py ) at the file on GitHub. To add or move a page: write it, add it to GROUPS in tools/docs.py , and run: python tools/docs.py # the menus and mkdocs.yml's nav python tools/docs.py --check # what CI runs: fails if they are out of date To see the site: pip install -r requirements-docs.txt mkdocs serve # http://127.0.0.1:8000 Publishing needs, once, Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Deploy from a branch: gh-pages , / (root) on GitHub.

docs.text: Features For: anyone deciding whether the page does what they need. You'll find: every feature in short, with a link to the details. sitelabs-graph-ui is a read-only web page for a graph server : run openCypher queries, and see the answer as a table, in 3D, in 2D or as JSON. It is what sitelabs-graph-database and sitelabs-partitioned-graph serve at /console . It is one HTML file and two libraries , with nothing to build and nothing fetched from the internet, so it works on a private network. A project keeps a pinned copy of a release ( Installing into a project ). Querying Queries with parameters , in a box, parameters as JSON. Run , or Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac). Read-only, always. Every query goes with "read_only": true , so the server refuses a write, whatever the API key may do ( Security ). Explain puts EXPLAIN before the query. The query box colours the language, completes keywords and, after a : , labels and types, and marks where a syntax error is ( The query box ). History: the last 50 queries in this browser, newest first; their text only, not their parameters ( History ). Labels and types beside the query: click one to see some of them ( The side panel ). Answers A table of the first 2,000 rows, JSON of the whole answer, and 3D and 2D graph views ( The answer ). The graph views draw the nodes, relationships and paths anywhere in the answer, coloured by first label. Hover for a label, click a node for all of it ( Graph views ). Expanding: click a node, then Expand neighbours , to add what it connects to, and carry on from there: the way to explore a graph too big to draw ( Expanding ). A size limit on what is drawn, and advice when a graph is too big to read ( How big a graph ). What a server adds A server says what it has in GET /console/config.json , and the page shows only that ( Server contract ): Feature What the page gets schema Counts of every label and type, and each type's properties, from GET /schema pages Answers 500 rows at a time, More rows , and Fetch more rows to draw profile Profile : the plan, and each round of partition calls with its time and sizes past As of a past load : reading the graph as it was after an earlier load cancel Cancel stops the running query Around the page Light and dark , following the system, with a button to switch. Works at phone width : the side panel goes above the query. Everything from the graph is escaped before it is shown, and the page works under a strict content security policy ( Security ). Tested in a real browser against a stand-in server, once with every feature and once with none ( Tests ). What it doesn't do Write. It is for reading and exploring; writes go through the server's API. Edit a server's data model, users or keys. Those belong to the server. Draw very large answers. What you can read runs out long before what the browser can draw ( How big a graph ).

docs.text: How big a graph For: developers choosing the page's limits, and anyone wondering why a big answer isn't drawn. You'll find: what was measured, on what, what it shows, and how the page's limits follow from it. What limits a graph is what you can read, long before what the browser can draw. What was measured On an Apple M2 laptop (Chrome, its GPU), on connected data of about 8 relationships per node, all of it drawn: Nodes, relationships View Layout While laid out Turning or panning Can you read it? 116, 794 3D 5.1 s 60 fps 60 fps Yes 2D 5.0 s 60 fps 61 fps Yes 1,052, 8,032 3D 4.0 s 31 fps 48 fps The clusters only, as a hairball 2D 2.0 s 61 fps 60 fps The clusters only, as a hairball 5,212, 40,198 3D 15.4 s 5 fps 7 fps No: a solid disc 2D 3.5 s 36 fps 55 fps No: a solid disc Layout is the time until the layout settles (the page records it in the stage's data-laid-out ). The two frame-rate columns are while it is settling and afterwards, moving round it. What it shows Around a hundred nodes read well in either view. Around a thousand still draw smoothly, in 2D especially, but show only the clusters. Five thousand draw (2D comfortably, 3D barely), and show nothing. Focused answers read well at any size of graph. It is the size of the answer that matters, not of the graph. The page's limits Limit Value Why Nodes drawn, by default 1,000 Where a picture stops showing more than clusters "Hard to read" advice over 500 nodes Before the hairball "3D is slow" advice over 2,000 nodes in 3D Between 31 and 5 fps Fewer details drawn over 1,000 nodes No arrows, shorter layout, coarser 3D Expanding 100 relationships a node One step at a time stays readable They are constants in ui/console.html ( describe() , draw() and EXPAND ). So expanding is the way into a big graph: start from one node and grow it ( Expanding a node ). Libraries that draw hundreds of thousands of points (cosmos.gl, for example) aren't worth adding for that reason. Measuring your own Draw an answer of the size you care about, in each view, and read: the layout time, from the line above the graph ("Laid out in N s"), or document.getElementById('stage').dataset.laidOut in the browser's console; the frame rate, from the browser's performance tools (in Chrome, Rendering → Frame rendering stats ), while it settles and while you turn or pan it. Say the machine, browser and data when adding a row to the table above.

docs.text: Graph views For: anyone drawing an answer. You'll find: what the 3D and 2D views draw and how, moving round them, the size limit, and expanding a node to explore. What is drawn The 3D tab uses 3d-force-graph (three.js, WebGL), the 2D tab force-graph (a canvas). Each is loaded from /console/vendor/ the first time its tab opens, so a page that only shows tables never loads them. The page looks through every value of every row, including lists and maps inside them, for: Value Recognised by Drawn as A node id , labels and properties A dot, coloured by its first label A relationship id , type , start and end A line with an arrow, start to end A path nodes and relationships Its nodes and relationships So RETURN n , RETURN a, r, b , RETURN p and RETURN collect(n) all draw. A query that returns only properties ( RETURN n.name ) has nothing to draw, and the view says so. A relationship whose ends the answer didn't return is drawn with grey placeholders for them, and the line above the graph counts them ("ends not in the answer"). Return the nodes too ( RETURN a, r, b ) to see them properly. Six colours go round the labels in the order they are met; the legend below the graph says which is which. Moving round 3D 2D Drag the background Turn Pan Scroll Zoom Zoom Drag a node Move it Move it Hover Its labels, and its name or title The same Click a node Everything about it, in a panel The same When the layout settles, the view zooms to fit. Switching tab or theme draws it again. Leaving a graph tab stops the drawing, so it doesn't keep the GPU busy. 3D needs WebGL; without it the tab says to use 2D. The size limit Draw up to sets the most nodes drawn: 100, 500, 1,000 (the default), 2,000, 5,000 or 10,000. The line above the graph says how many of how many nodes and relationships are drawn, and gives advice past the sizes that stop being readable: over 500 nodes: narrow the query (labels, properties, LIMIT ); over 2,000 in 3D: 3D is slow at this size, try 2D. Past 1,000 nodes the views draw less to keep up: no arrows, a shorter layout, and in 3D coarser dots and fainter lines. The numbers behind these limits are in How big a graph . With pages , an answer may have more rows than were fetched. Fetch more rows to draw fetches pages of 5,000 until there are ten times the limit (enough for the nodes and most of their relationships), or none are left. Expanding a node To explore a graph too big to draw, start small and grow it: Run a query for one node or a few, for example MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p . Open 3D or 2D , and click a node. Click Expand neighbours . The page sends: cypher MATCH (a)-[r]-(b) WHERE id(a) = $id RETURN a, r, b LIMIT 100 with the node's id, read-only, and adds what comes back beside it. The node is drawn larger, and the button says Expanded . 4. Click a new node and expand it, and so on. What was expanded: is always drawn , whatever the size limit: it was asked for by hand; stays when you switch between 3D and 2D; goes with the next query, or with Back to the answer . A node with more than 100 relationships shows its first 100, and says so.

docs.text: Installing into a project For: developers of a project that serves the page, and whoever releases it. You'll find: installing a copy, checking it, its manifest, and changing the page and releasing it. A project keeps a pinned copy of a release in its own repository, with a manifest of its version and files' hashes, which the project's tests check. It needs no submodule or package, and builds offline. Installing and checking From a checkout of this repository, beside the project's: python install.py ../sitelabs-partitioned-graph/app/static/graph-ui # replaces the copy python install.py --check ../sitelabs-partitioned-graph/app/static/graph-ui # is it this release? install.py needs the standard library only. Installing replaces the target with a copy of ui/ , and writes MANIFEST.json . It refuses a folder that has files and no MANIFEST.json , so it never replaces what it didn't install. Checking changes nothing. It says what differs (the version, or a file changed, added or missing) and exits 1, or says the target is this release and exits 0. A project's tests compare the copy against it, so an edit made there fails them: don't edit the copies. Changing the page Change ui/console.html here, and its tests ( Tests ). docs.text: Security For: developers of the page and of servers that serve it, and whoever reviews them. You'll find: what keeps the page read-only, how it handles what comes from the graph, the policy it runs under, what it keeps in the browser, and what it leaves to the server. Read-only Every query the page sends, from the query box, the side panel or expanding, has "read_only": true . The server must refuse a write with it, whatever the API key may do , so a key with write access can't change the graph through the page. The page doesn't try to spot writes itself: the server decides. What comes from the graph Labels, types, property names and values, error messages and the server's title are all data that someone else may have written. The page: escapes them ( & , < , > , " ) before putting them into HTML, or sets them as text; escapes the graph views' hover labels, which the libraries put into HTML; builds the query box's colouring from escaped text, so HTML typed or pasted into it is shown, not run (a test checks this). Clicking a label or type puts its name into a query in backticks. A name holding a backtick makes a query that fails; it is still sent read-only. The content security policy A server serves the page with: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none' Part Means default-src 'self' , connect-src 'self' Nothing is loaded from, or sent to, anywhere but the server script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' The page's own script and the two libraries from /console/vendor/ . No eval : the libraries work without it style-src 'unsafe-inline' The page's own styles img-src 'self' data: blob: The libraries' canvases and textures frame-ancestors 'none' No other site can put the page in a frame The libraries are served from a fixed list of two names, so the vendor path can't serve any other file. Add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff to both. The API key The page itself needs no key. Queries do, when the server needs one. The key is typed into the page, sent as X-API-Key with each request, and kept in this browser's localStorage ( graph-ui.key ), so it is there on the next visit. Anyone who can use that browser profile, or run script on the server's origin, can read it. Clear it from the field (it is saved when changed) on a shared machine. Where the server has keys that can only read, use one in the page. The page can't write with any key, but a key kept in a browser may leak, and a read-only one limits what it can then do elsewhere. History The history keeps the text of the last 50 queries in localStorage , not their parameters, which may be private: put private values in parameters, not in the query. Clear forgets them. What the server must do The page is a client: what protects the graph is the server. Refuse writes when read_only is true. Check X-API-Key on POST /opencypher , GET /schema and the other API paths; /console , /console/config.json and /console/vendor/* need none and hold nothing private. Serve the page over HTTPS anywhere but a developer's own machine: the key goes with every request. Limit how long a query may run and how many rows it may answer; the page asks for at most 5,000 rows a page, but doesn't enforce anything.

docs.text: Server contract For: developers of a server that serves the page. You'll find: every path the page calls, every field it sends and reads, and what each optional feature adds. The page calls only its own server ( connect-src 'self' ), at these paths. Every call sends Content-Type: application/json , and X-API-Key when a key has been typed. An answer that isn't 2xx is shown as <status>: <error> , from its error field, or its whole body when that isn't JSON. Always Path What GET /console console.html , with the content security policy . Needs no key: the page asks for one GET /console/config.json What the server has ( below ) GET /console/vendor/<file> 3d-force-graph.min.js and force-graph.min.js , and no other file. Called the first time a graph tab opens POST /opencypher Queries ( below ) /console/config.json {"title": "Graph console", "schema": true, "pages": true, "profile": true, "past": true, "cancel": true} title names the page and its tab. Each other field turns on a feature ; a missing one is off. When the file can't be fetched, every feature is off and the title is "Graph console". POST /opencypher The request: Field When What query Always The query text; with Explain , EXPLAIN and the query params Always The parameters, as a JSON object ( {} when there are none) read_only Always true . The server must refuse a write, with a 400 page_size With pages 500 profile With profile , on Profile true at_load With past , when a load is given The load number Headers: X-API-Key (when typed), and X-Request-ID: console-<8 hex digits> on each query from the query box, for cancel . The answer: {"columns": ["a", "r"], "rows": [{"a": {"id": "1", "labels": ["Person"], "properties": {"name": "Ann"}}, "r": {"id": "7", "type": "KNOWS", "start": "1", "end": "2", "properties": {}}}], "stats": {"rounds": 2, "calls": 4}} Field What columns The column names, in order rows One object a row, keyed by column stats Optional. With rounds and calls , the status line shows them cursor With pages : the next page's cursor, or absent/null on the last profile With profile , when asked for ( below ) The values the page draws and shows specially: Value Shape A node {"id", "labels", "properties"} A relationship {"id", "type", "start", "end", "properties"} : start and end are node ids A path {"nodes", "relationships"} : lists of the above Ids may be strings or numbers, but must be the same for a node and the relationships that refer to it, and must not be 0 or "" : the graph views skip a value whose id is empty or zero. An error: a non-2xx status and {"error": "..."} . When the message holds offset N (a character offset into the query), the page marks the query there. What the page's own queries need Query Needs CALL db.labels() YIELD label RETURN label Without schema : the labels, a row each CALL db.relationshipTypes() YIELD relationshipType RETURN relationshipType Without schema : the relationship types MATCH (n:`L`) RETURN n LIMIT 25 Clicking a label or node type MATCH (a)-[r:`T`]->(b) RETURN a, r, b LIMIT 25 Clicking a relationship type MATCH (a)-[r]-(b) WHERE id(a) = $id RETURN a, r, b LIMIT 100 Expanding; id() must take the node's id as the answer gives it Optional features schema GET /schema answers: {"load": 12, "nodes": 1000, "relationships": 8000, "labels": [{"name": "Person", "count": 1000}], "node_types": [{"name": "Person", "count": 1000, "properties": [{"name": "name", "type": "str"}]}], "relationship_types": [{"name": "KNOWS", "count": 8000, "properties": []}]} pages page_size in the request, cursor in the answer, and GET /opencypher/cursors/{cursor} answering {"rows", "cursor"} for the next page. Fetch more rows to draw adds ?page_size=5000 . profile "profile": true in the request; the answer's profile : {"seconds": {"total": 0.012, "partitions": 0.009, "coordinator": 0.003}, "plan": ["NodeScan(p:Person)", "Expand(p)-[:KNOWS]->(q)"], "rounds": [{"round": 1, "call": ["scan"], "partitions": [0, 1], "sent": 0, "received": 120, "seconds": 0.004}]} The shape is sitelabs-partitioned-graph's (the plan's lines above are only an illustration): a server without partitions would turn this off. past at_load in the request: read the graph as it was after that load. cancel DELETE /queries/{id} , with the X-Request-ID the query was sent with. Whatever the query's own request then answers (usually an error) is shown as usual; an error from the DELETE is shown too. sitelabs-graph-database turns every feature off; sitelabs-partitioned-graph turns every one on.

docs.text: Serving it For: developers of a server that serves the page. You'll find: the steps, an example in FastAPI, and how to check it works. A server needs three small routes for the page, and an openCypher endpoint the page can call. In sitelabs-partitioned-graph and sitelabs-graph-database these are about 30 lines, in app/routers/console.py . Every request and answer is in the Server contract . Step by step Install a copy of a release into the project, for example into app/static/graph-ui ( Installing into a project ). Serve the page at GET /console : console.html , with the content security policy . It needs no key. Say what the server has at GET /console/config.json : its title, and which of schema , pages , profile , past and cancel it has. Serve the two libraries at GET /console/vendor/<file> : 3d-force-graph.min.js and force-graph.min.js , and no other file. Answer queries at POST /opencypher , refusing a write when read_only is true. Test it against the server ( below ). An example, in FastAPI from pathlib import Path from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, HTMLResponse router = APIRouter(include_in_schema=False) UI = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "static" / "graph-ui" # the installed copy VENDOR = ("3d-force-graph.min.js", "force-graph.min.js") CONFIG = {"title": "Graph console", "schema": True, "pages": True, "profile": False, "past": False, "cancel": True} CSP = ("default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; " "img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'") @router.get("/console", response_class=HTMLResponse) def console() -> HTMLResponse: return HTMLResponse((UI / "console.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), headers={"Content-Security-Policy": CSP, "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff"}) @router.get("/console/config.json") def config() -> dict: return CONFIG @router.get("/console/vendor/{name}") def vendor(name: str) -> FileResponse: if name not in VENDOR: # these two, and no other file raise HTTPException(404, f"no file {name!r}") return FileResponse(UI / "vendor" / name, media_type="text/javascript", headers={"Cache-Control": "public, max-age=86400", "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff"}) sitelabs-partitioned-graph's app/routers/console.py is this, with every feature on. Choosing the features Turn on only what the server really does: the page sends the extra fields and calls the extra paths of each one it is told about. Feature Turn it on when the server has schema GET /schema with counts and properties pages page_size on POST /opencypher , a cursor in the answer, and GET /opencypher/cursors/{cursor} profile "profile": true , answered with the partitioned-graph profile shape past at_load : reading the graph as it was after a past load cancel DELETE /queries/{id} , with the id from X-Request-ID A server with none of them still gets the whole page apart from those; the labels and types then come from CALL db.labels() and CALL db.relationshipTypes() . Without a config.json at all (a 404, or no answer) the page treats every feature as off. Checking it works Open /console , and check the title, the side panel's lists, and that the browser's console shows no errors and no content-security-policy refusals. Run MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) RETURN a, r, b LIMIT 25 , and open 3D and 2D . Run CREATE (:Test) : it must be refused. In the project's own tests: check the installed copy is the release ( python install.py --check ), and that each route answers as above. sitelabs-partitioned-graph also runs this page in a browser against itself.

docs.text: Tests For: developers of the page. You'll find: running the tests, the stand-in server, what each test checks, what CI runs, and what isn't tested. Running them pip install playwright pytest && playwright install chromium python -m pytest Without Playwright, or without a browser, only the install is tested and the rest are skipped. With REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 (as in CI) a missing browser fails the run instead, so a broken setup can't pass by skipping. The stand-in server tests/test_ui.py starts a small http.server on a free port for each test. It serves the page with the content security policy , the libraries, a config.json and GET /schema , and answers POST /opencypher by the query's start: Query Answer CALL db.labels() , CALL db.relationshipTypes() Person , KNOWS CREATE ... 400, read-only One with $id (expanding) Ann, KNOWS, and a new node, Bob ONE ... One node, Ann BAD ... 400, a syntax error at offset 4 Anything else Ann, and a KNOWS to a node not in the answer It records every request it gets, so a test can check what the page sent. Two configs: FULL , every feature on, and PLAIN , none. docs.text: Using the page For: anyone exploring a graph by hand: analysts, developers, whoever runs the server. You'll find: opening the page, what each part does, the keys, and where it keeps things. Opening it The server serves the page at /console , for example http://127.0.0.1:5050/console for sitelabs-partitioned-graph. The page needs no key to open. If the server needs one for queries, type it into API key at the top: it goes with every request as X-API-Key , and is remembered in this browser ( Security ). The title is the server's, from its config.json . Buttons for features the server doesn't have ( Profile , Cancel , as of a past load ) aren't shown. The side panel On the left (above the query at phone width): The totals : nodes, relationships and the current load, when the server has schema . Labels , Node types (with schema ) and Relationship types . With schema , each has its count, and each type its properties ( name: type ). Click one to run a query that shows some of them: cypher MATCH (n:`Person`) RETURN n LIMIT 25 MATCH (a)-[r:`KNOWS`]->(b) RETURN a, r, b LIMIT 25 Without schema , the lists come from CALL db.labels() and CALL db.relationshipTypes() , with no counts. * History ( below ). Changing the API key loads the lists again. The query box The page starts with a query that counts the nodes by label. The box: Colours keywords, strings, numbers, $parameters , :Labels and // comments . Completes as you type: keywords after two letters, and labels and relationship types after a : (from the side panel). Up to eight suggestions; ↑ and ↓ choose, Tab or Enter accepts, Escape closes them. Marks a syntax error with a wavy underline, when the server's message says offset N . Typing clears it. Key What it does Ctrl+Enter, ⌘+Enter Run Tab Accept a suggestion; otherwise indent by two spaces Escape, then Tab Leave the box (for moving round the page by keyboard) ↑, ↓ Move between suggestions Parameters go in the box below, as JSON: {"name": "Ann"} . A query refers to them as $name . JSON that doesn't parse stops the run with a message. Running Button Sends Run The query, its parameters, and "read_only": true to POST /opencypher Profile (with profile ) The same with "profile": true ; the answer opens on the Profile tab Explain EXPLAIN and the query: the plan, without running it Cancel (with cancel ) DELETE /queries/{id} for the running query as of a past load (with past ) A load number, sent as at_load : the graph as it was then The status line, on the right, shows how long it took (in the browser, so network included), the rounds and calls when the server reports them, and the number of rows, or "more rows" when there are more pages to fetch. An error from the server shows in red, with its HTTP status. The answer Tab What it shows Table The first 2,000 rows. A node is (:Label) {properties} , a relationship [:TYPE] {properties} , a path its number of hops 3D , 2D The nodes, relationships and paths in the answer, drawn ( Graph views ) JSON The whole answer as the server sent it, made only when the tab is opened, and cut at 5 MB Profile (with profile ) The total time, split between waiting for the partitions and the coordinator; the plan; every round of calls with the partitions, rows sent and received, and its time With pages , the page asks for 500 rows at a time, and More rows fetches the next page. History The last 50 queries run in this browser, newest first, with no repeats. Click one to put it in the box (it doesn't run). Clear forgets them all. It keeps their text only, not their parameters, which may be private. A query is remembered when it is run, whether it worked or not. What it keeps in the browser All in localStorage , for this server's address only: Key What graph-ui.key The API key, as typed graph-ui.history The history: a JSON list of query texts graph-ui.theme light or dark , once the ◐ button has been used; otherwise the system's When the browser won't store (a private window, blocked site data), the page still works and forgets them on leaving.
